title: Violent birth announcement from an infant star
caption: The young star IRAS 14568-6304 in the Circinus molecular cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Circinus, IRAS 14568-6304 · constellation Circinus · about 2500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA Acknowledgements: R. Sahai (Jet Propulsion Laboratory), Serge Meunier

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A young star wrapped in a haze of golden gas and dust sits within a sweeping curve of darkness that hides the sky behind it. The star is IRAS 14568-6304, and a tail extends below it. The dark swoosh is the Circinus molecular cloud.

That cloud holds around 250 000 times the Sun's mass in gas, dust and young stars. Two huge clumps within it, nicknamed Circinus-West and Circinus-East, are its leading star-forming sites. IRAS 14568-6304 lies under a blurry fog inside Circinus-West.

The tail is a protostellar jet. Most of the material a new star gathers from its parent cloud goes into the star and its accretion disc, which may one day form planets. But at some stage the star began flinging some of it into space at supersonic speeds. Jets like this give astronomers valuable clues about how stars form.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.31 x 1.53 arcminutes) and distance (2500 light years), the frame spans roughly 2.4 × 1.1 light-years. Its light set out about 2,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys imaged this region through visible and near-infrared filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of the light is near-infrared, invisible to the eye, and the faint golden haze would be far too dim to see directly.

explore: Each of the two big clumps holds roughly 5000 solar masses. Several stars in Circinus-West drive outflows, IRAS 14568-6304 among them, and together they form an outflow ranking among the most energetic, most massive and brightest yet reported. Some scientists have suggested calling Circinus-West the nest of molecular outflows. Serge Meunier entered a version of this image in the Hubble's Hidden Treasures competition.
alt: A young star in a golden haze of gas and dust with a tail below it, set in a curving band of dark cloud.
